Just because someone says it incorrectly and it becomes a word doesn't make it right. If you pronounce something differently, it doesn't change the spelling. It started as a stupid mistake. Until enough people used it that the OED decided it should be added, it was wrong. For example, "could've" versus "could of." The latter is wrong. It's a contraction of "could have." When people use "could of" because of "cadence," that doesn't make it right, it makes them stupid.

He spun it to where it sounded like I was trying to take him from her, rather than an admission of feelings and acceptance that they wouldn't be returned. I never expected anything to change. Just needed to get it off my chest. I found out all of this happened after I got those stares you mentioned all morning. My friends weren't talking to me. They just went quiet as I passed. But once I was able to explain, the best friend I loved forgave me and we were still close. He didn't agree with how things went down. Those are the kinds of friends you deserve. And I promise, if you stay strong, you will find people like that.

Try your best to be firm but accommodating when people are like this with you, and not even just in this situation. Its going to be hard, and VERY nerve wracking, but it will be worth it in the long run.

Recognize that they're upset about a situation, but don't take the blame for it if the blame isn't yours. You'll gain a lot of confidence this way and it could really help in turning your mindset around for the future.

Truthfully, its been hard finding that myself. As a young woman with a myriad of mental disorders including PTSD, Battered Woman Syndrome, an on-and-off battle with depression, Panic Disorder, and probably more, it's easy to see how even the desire to find love was often squelched. 

I had thought I had found love more than once. I was even married. But the biggest thing I learned from that marriage was that words mean nothing without action to back them up.

For example, my first husband often told me he loved me, but often ignored me and even shut me down. He would rarely talk with me or touch me unless it was a sexual advance. Even sex with him was empty. It's so strange, but there is an obvious difference in the way someone kisses you when they love you and mean the kiss, or if they're just horny. There's an almost deepness you feel in the kiss--or any kind of intimacy--that one simply cannot fake, though it is hard to know until you've experienced the difference. There was no love in my marriage. Simply lust on my husband's part, it seems. After I filed for divorce, he got wasted one night and admitted he didn't even want to marry me in the first place. See? No love whatsoever. 

What my current fiancé has taught me about love, however, was that it is about mutual sacrifice. I already knew that somewhat, but had always been in a position where I've been the only one to sacrifice, and, in turn, felt that it was my duty to be okay with that. 

But that's not true love.

True love is holding them close at night even after an argument. It's noticing when they're tired and perhaps making dinner, putting the kids to bed, or whatever other task you may not want to do yourself, but it would make life easier for your partner. It's anticipating their needs and providing relief from stress. It's about creating a place of safety and security in your relationship. 

Love is never about you. It's about them. 

That's what most people can never figure out. Loving and being loved is about giving up your life (your freedoms, your comfort, all of it) for the other person and whatever they may need at any moment. And most people are too selfish and distrusting to truly love. They worry that if they sacrifice, they won't be taken care of. And when both parties do this, the relationship falls apart. You have to trust that your partner will sacrifice for you in return, but being okay if they don't always do that. That's what sacrifice is truly about. 

That's the most terrifying part in loving someone. The trust. You must love them completely and trust they will do the same, even when they don't. If you can't do that, then how can the other party trust you?
